what: Problem statement P1 (ad placement). Hardest, most AI-native, closest to hoichoi revenue, fits Go pipeline skills. Assets folder confirms it is the expected track.
Modular monolith, one Go binary, in-process event bus, one Cloud Run instance (max-instances=1).
Hosting: Cloud Run + GCS bucket + Neon Postgres, Rs 300 budget alert. Render free too weak for ffmpeg, HF Docker Spaces now paid, Supabase free pauses during judging window.
AI: Whisper large-v3 on Groq for speech timing; Gemini (Flash-Lite bulk, Flash final) for judgment. Model names resolved via ListModels and printed at startup, never hardcoded from memory.

Speech guard needs two signals: Whisper segment spans + margin, then Gemini audio check on survivors. silencedetect dropped (background score defeats amplitude thresholds; Whisper under-detects Bengali speech).
Pipeline order: shots -> scenes (cheap keyframe pass) -> candidates -> hard filters -> AI scoring on survivors -> pacing optimizer -> brand match. Pacing is an optimizer, not a pre-filter.
Frontend is React (Vite) built to dist/ and embedded with go:embed. Same origin, no CORS, SPA fallback.
Uploads go browser -> GCS via signed resumable URL (Cloud Run caps request bodies at 32 MiB). Processing is async, job id + polling.
Ad creatives are not in the assets; generate slates with ffmpeg at exact 15/20/30s durations. Runtime image needs fonts.
Pacing rules are not given in the brief; defaults are explicit config, printed at startup and shown in UI and debug JSON.
Sample results precomputed by the same pipeline, cached by content hash, with Re-run live. Never hard-coded.

Frontend lives in web/ with web/embed.go (package web), because go:embed cannot reach parent directories. HTTP layer is internal/server. Module dirs are created when their code lands, not as empty stubs.
Log format switched to LOG.jsonl (one JSON object per line) so it stays append-only and machine readable. Docs folder may hold any file type as long as it is aligned and verified (Aranya, 14:15).

Handbook re-read via Notion (P1 toggle + FAQ). Matches pasted text. Debug JSON is a required pipeline output. No pacing numbers anywhere, so config defaults stand: 4 breaks/hour, 6m gap, 15% ad load, 3m head, 2m tail, 500ms speech margin.
Scene segmentation is a judged output (blind-viewing check). UI and debug JSON expose the scene list with boundaries, duration, description, dominant activity.
Scene boundaries: colour histogram + transcript gaps propose, one AI call per scene describes it and confirms or merges ambiguous boundaries. Deterministic fallback if AI fails.
Break selection is a DP over (candidate, break count) with a minimum score threshold, respecting min gap, max per hour, ad load, head/tail margins. Not greedy, not plain weighted interval scheduling.
Local tooling without sudo: Postgres 17 in Docker (container adbreak-pg, port 5432), static ffmpeg 7.0.2 in ~/.local/bin. Deploy image will apt install ffmpeg.
Sample episodes probed: all 960x540 h264, AAC 48k stereo. Durations 20.5 to 25.9 min, mandaar 39.2 min at 24fps.
Workflow: feature branch + PR per task, GitHub Actions (go vet, go test, web build in parallel jobs), merge via gh when green. Public repo thisizaro/adbreak. Deployment deferred until Aranya is back.
Keys verified live: Groq lists whisper-large-v3 and -turbo; Gemini lists 2.5-flash, 3.1-flash-lite, 3.8-flash. ASR model and Gemini models are separate config vars, printed at startup.
why: .env GROQ_MODEL is a chat model (gpt-oss-20b), ASR needs its own var.

what: ARCHITECTURE.md added: modules, pipeline funnel, brand matching, upload sequence, deployment. AI provider is its own package internal/ai (shared by scenes, breaks, brands) instead of living inside scenes; blob storage is internal/blob; slates is its own package.
why: Three modules call the LLM, so the provider seam belongs in one place.

what: Default max breaks/hour changed 4 -> 6. Break budget = min(floor(duration_h * rate), floor(ad_load * duration / pod_seconds)). Added PACING_POD_SECONDS=30 (worst-case pod for ad-load math) and PACING_MIN_SCORE=0.35 (the whether threshold).
why: At 4/h every 20-26 min sample episode gets only 1 break (floor 1.37). 6/h gives 2, mandaar 3, still well inside 15% ad load.

what: Whisper large-v3 timestamps on Bengali are coarse: segments cover 92.8% of bhojon_bilashi and are contiguous; 54 words longer than 2s (max 29.5s) absorb music and silence.
why: Whisper pads segments through non-speech in low-resource languages.
fix: Keep conservative guard (segment OR word span + 500ms margin): 29 of 398 cuts survive, enough for 2-3 breaks. Gemini audio check on survivors is the second signal. Silero VAD noted as a future improvement, not built.

what: Log timestamps 14:24-14:28 were estimated ahead of the real clock.
fix: Corrected in place once; all entries now take time from `date`.

what: First real end-to-end run on bhojon_bilashi: 399 shots -> 398 candidates -> 25 pass hard filters -> 8 pass AI speech check -> budget 2 -> 1 selected (6m gap) -> placed brand_a (cooking/spices, fit 1.0), brand_b blocked (eating unsure). 8 Gemini calls, 42.8k tokens, 2m50s.
why: AI audio check rejected 17 of 25 cuts Whisper thought were silent, confirming the two-signal guard is needed.

what: johnvansickle static ffmpeg 7.0.2 has no drawtext filter; slate render failed with No such filter.
fix: Local dev uses BtbN static ffmpeg n8.1 (has freetype). Deploy image uses Debian ffmpeg, which ships drawtext. Slate text passed via textfile= so runtime brand names never need filtergraph escaping.

what: Vertical slice verified in headless Chromium (Playwright): library -> episode -> Play 6s before -> content paused at exactly 917.0s, Brand A slate on with badge -> slate end -> content resumed at 917.04s playing. Player schedules ads by parsing the VMAP, not the debug JSON. scripts/e2e.cjs keeps the check repeatable.
why: Aranya rule: verify on the actual screen, not by exit code.

what: Gemini free tier quota exhausted: GenerateRequestsPerDayPerProjectPerModel-FreeTier = 20 requests/day for gemini-2.5-flash. Batch runs of 5 episodes plus scene windows hit it; runs failed with 429 after backoff.
why: Free tier daily cap is per model and tiny; a single episode needs ~10-15 calls.
fix: Dev switched to GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-3.1-flash-lite via env (separate quota), scene window 30 -> 80 shots. BLOCKER for demo: judges uploading held-out videos need a billing-enabled key. Needs Aranya decision.

what: Candidates stay at shot cuts but scene context shapes the score: within -15s/+20s of an AI scene boundary +0.1 (near_scene_boundary), otherwise x0.6 (mid_scene). Exact-boundary-only candidates gave bhojon_bilashi zero breaks because presenter narration runs across every transition. Also mediaResolution LOW on all Gemini calls: image cost 1102 -> 266 tokens.

ARCHITECTURE.md sections 1 and 2 updated to match code: added pipeline (stage order + cache) and library (read side) packages; jobs/store/blob still planned; pipeline diagram shows scene stage and scene-context scoring.

9th brand verified live with zero code change: added brand_i (security/home safety) to a copy of the catalogue; on mohanagar it won the night-street surveillance break at 888.9s (fit 0.6, beat brand_e) and scored 0.1 at the restaurant break. Placement cache is keyed by catalogue hash, so only placement re-ran (2 calls). Default 8-brand result restored from cache.

Dockerfile: node:24-trixie-slim builds SPA, golang:1.27-trixie builds static binary with SPA embedded, debian:trixie-slim runtime with ffmpeg + fonts-dejavu-core, USER nobody. Verified locally: drawtext present, slate rendered in-container in 1.9s, API and SPA served.
why: Trixie is current Debian stable; same font path as dev. Open item for deploy: DATA_DIR must be writable by nobody (Cloud Run: /tmp or GCS via blob seam).

what: Async jobs built: internal/jobs (in-process bus, single worker = one job at a time), POST /api/uploads -> PUT upload_url -> POST /api/jobs -> GET /api/jobs/{id}; upload validated by ffprobe (needs audio, <= MAX_UPLOAD_SECONDS 3600, <= MAX_UPLOAD_MB 700). Verified live via curl and in headless Chromium (upload -> live stage log -> auto-navigate to result). Job state is in memory; upload URL is local until the GCS blob seam lands.

what: From Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI; API still aiplatform.googleapis.com) we use only Models: Gemini generateContent. Not Agent Studio, ADK, Deployments (Agent Engine), RAG Engine or Vector Search. Auth via Application Default Credentials (user ADC locally, Cloud Run service account in prod), no key files.
why: Pipeline is fixed stages with structured calls and code-enforced rules; an agent runtime adds nondeterminism and cost where the brief punishes mistakes (negative contexts, mid-dialogue cuts).
